division.heading: Lawyers’ Charges, Retainer Agreements and Right of Review

operative_text.controlling:
10.25   On application by a client, the Court may order a lawyer to
deliver to a person named in the order any record of the client
under the lawyer’s control.

BOOK_A.title: Order to Return Records
BOOK_A.commentary:
The former solicitor for an estate would not (after a while) answer correspondence or even
cooperate in service of papers, so the court ordered that the papers be turned over to the new
solicitor.⁴

There is a discussion of whether the client or the lawyer owns any given papers on the ﬁle of
that lawyer. That the paper in question was created by work for which that solicitor charged that
client is not conclusive. References to internal memos and communications should not be read
literally, and should be conﬁned to topics administrative or for the sole assistance of the law ﬁrm.
Many papers will have been created for more than one purpose, and then one should see which
was the dominant purpose. Ownership between principal and agent is not the test. There are few
bright lines.¹

footnotes.text: Quite similar to previous 1968 R.649. It came from 1914 R.779 (amended by O. C.1590-36), and 1944 C. R. 782. Cf. (Imp. ) 6 & 7 Vict. c.73 s.37, 7th para.
CPC Networks Corp. v. McDougall Gauley 2023 SKCA 90 (Aug 10) (¶’s 15-37). A set of 6 rules is given in ¶ 37: ibid.

BOOK_A.commentary_review_flag: Read in full, p.10-38 (line 1836) to p.10-39 (line 1864): title (line 1836), rule text (lines 1837-1838; marker '3' after 'lawyer's control.'), Related Provisions (lines 1840-1841: '2.28 (change of lawyer) ; 5.13 (obtaining records from others)'), and the note (lines 1843-1845 on p.10-38 and lines 1858-1863 after the page marker 10-39 at line 1856) with footnotes: p.10-38 fns 3 and 4 (block from line 1847; fns 1-2 belong to the 10.24 note) and p.10-39 fn 1 (line 1896, in the block after the text of 10.26) = 3. The lines after the note, 'Subdivision 5 / Appeal from Review Officer's Decision' (lines 1865-1866), are the division heading that precedes 10.26. Read against the official text: the rule text equals official 10.25 (EXACT_MATCH, no differences); the Related Provisions labels '2.28 (change of lawyer)' and '5.13 (obtaining records from others)' are labels for official 2.28 ('Change in lawyer of record or self-representation') and 5.13 ('Obtaining records from others'), and the Part 2 and Part 5 Related Provisions list 10.25 in return. The note is case-law summary, not the rule: the former estate solicitor who would not cooperate (fn 4 Re Marchuk Est. 2006 ABQB 24); 'There is a discussion of whether the client or the lawyer owns any given papers on the file of that lawyer ... Ownership between principal and agent is not the test. There are few bright lines.' (fn 1 of p.10-39: CPC Networks Corp. v. McDougall Gauley 2023 SKCA 90, Saskatchewan Court of Appeal, paras 15-37, 'A set of 6 rules is given in ¶ 37: ibid.'; the Part 5 note cites the same case as 2021 SKCA 127, combined_rule5.txt line 2373). Official 10.25 says nothing on ownership of papers; the six 'rules' of ¶ 37 are not printed. History fn 3: 'Quite similar to previous 1968 R.649. It came from 1914 R.779 (amended by O. C.1590-36), and 1944 C. R. 782. Cf. (Imp.) 6 & 7 Vict. c.73 s.37, 7th para.' - the 10.12 history (p.10-28 fn 7, line 1379) also cites '1914 R.779' and 'O. C.1590-36'; the note is not corroborated by Book B or Book C, which print no history. supra/infra: no supra or infra is used in this note. Printed as is: 'Re Marchuk Est.2006 ABQB 24'; 'CPC Networks Corp. v. McDougall Gauley 2023 SKCA 90 (Aug 10)'.
